title: Vehicle-to-infrastructure IEEE 802.11ad Wi-Fi dataset
authors: Mateus Mattos; António Rodrigues; Rui Meireles; Ana Aguiar
locator: Sections 2–3, Data description and experimental design; references 1, 5 and 6
evidence: The authors identify a separate control network for NTP, a one-car V2I setup, a third radio for over-the-air capture, GPS time, and application-level differential timing. The file tables above quantify the time-field discrepancy independently.

title: SLATE-PTP: A spine–leaf architecture timestamps and evaluation dataset for IEEE 1588 precision time protocol benchmarking
authors: Alberto Ortega; Víctor Vázquez; Jesús González; Eduardo Ros; Manuel Rodríguez-Álvarez

title: WiLi - Vehicular Wireless Channel Dataset enriched with LiDAR and Radar Data
authors: Benjamin Rainer; Stefan Zelenbaba; Anja Dakic; Markus Hofer; David Loschenbrand; Thomas Zemen; Xiaochun Ye; Guo Nan; Stefan Teschl; Peter Priller
locator: Section II, Figures 1–2, Tables I–II, measurement description
evidence: Two moving vehicles with GPS-synchronized MK5 radios, channel sounders, and ego-vehicle LiDAR/radar. Rx reports include sequence number, GPS time, and signal/noise. Table I has internal run-count conflicts for V2V scenario 2 (23 vs 17+4) and scenario 3 (15 vs 17+4).
rights_and_limitations: Public landing page reachable; linked Nextcloud share returned HTTP 503 in this run. Paper mentions Creative Commons without specifying the variant. Counts remain paper-level evidence.

title: Data accuracy in Vehicle-to-X cooperative awareness messages: An experimental study for the first commercial deployment of C-ITS in Europe
authors: Maximilian Bauder; Andreas Festag; Tibor Kubjatko; Hans-Georg Schweiger
evidence: Compares CAM contents with independent 100 Hz vehicle dynamics reference. CAM generation time is modulo 65,536 ms and the receiver timestamps via ROS/NTP; observed discrepancy includes receive processing.
rights_and_limitations: Publisher version CC BY 4.0. Raw data available on request. A receiver time difference alone cannot isolate radio delay.

title: Post-Processing Kalman Filter Application for Improving Cooperative Awareness Messages’ Position Data Accuracy
authors: Maximilian Bauder; Robin Langer; Tibor Kubjatko; Hans-Georg Schweiger
locator: methods on asynchronous CAM reception and interpolation; Conclusions; reference 8; Data Availability
evidence: Non-equidistant CAM timestamps and maneuvers change performance of offline filtering; reference vehicle data permits comparison. The authors identify limits of using one filter parametrization across scenarios.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY 4.0 publication. Underlying study data available on request.
